root_cause: REGRESSION introduced by Fix round 2 (iteration 3 -> 4). The golden's turn-2 caller supplies the passcode INLINE with the request ('...can you cancel it? Passcode is Sunset.'), and the golden expects lookup_accounts_by_caller + verify_passcode + cancel_alarm all chained in that one turn. In iteration 3 the agent opportunistically consumed the inline passcode and chained the whole flow; it passed. Fix round 2 added emphatic strict-sequential, ask-then-STOP-and-wait language to Resolve_Account ('The confirmation question MUST be a standalone turn ... then STOP and wait ... do NOT ask for the passcode in the same message — the passcode request comes only AFTER the caller confirms the branch') plus a new Verify_Passcode step-5 pushback path. Although that standalone-turn language is scoped to multi-branch disambiguation, it reinforced a one-question-per-turn disposition that bled into this single-account path. Combined with Verify_Passcode step 1 ('Ask the caller for the account passcode'), which is unconditional and never tells the agent to reuse an inline-supplied passcode, the agent now stops after lookup and asks 'Could you please provide the passcode for verification?' — discarding the passcode the caller already gave. The golden's next user turn ('No, that's everything. Thanks.') is then read as a decline/closing, so the agent jumps to Closing + end_session, never calling verify_passcode or cancel_alarm. Surface symptom is TOOL_MISSING cancel_alarm; the deeper break is verify_passcode being dropped one turn earlier. Forward-narrowing fix: add an explicit carve-out so the agent uses a passcode the caller has already supplied (do not re-ask), and scope the 'ask-then-stop / do not ask passcode in same message' language to the multi-branch disambiguation case only — do not let it suppress chaining when the account is single AND the passcode is already in hand.
